description:
From software engineers to agronomists, we’re a team that looks beyond pure code and technical specs. We want to connect high-end satellite data directly to the hands of farmers facing real climate shifts.

We are actively looking for teammates in UX/Frontend, geospatial data visualization/maps, Machine Learning, and agribusiness/agronomy. Join us to turn orbital data into real harvest resilience!
summary:
RasterRoot is a mobile, user-friendly and easy to use decision-support application designed to help farmers plan the crop rotation strategies. 
By integrating NASA Earth observation data, local farm information, and agronomic criteria, the platform uses a multi-criteria analysis model to recommend sustainable and productive cropping systems. 
Farmers can map fields, and with the app evaluation of the climate and water conditions, compare different rotation scenarios based on factors such as water availability, soil health, erosion risk, crop diversification, vegetation cover, operational feasibility, and economic potential. 
Initially focused on Uberlândia and the Triângulo Mineiro region in Brazil, RasterRoot aims to transform complex scientific data into accessible insights that support better agricultural decisions. 
The project promotes sustainable land management, increases resilience to climate change, and helps producers balance productivity with environmental conservation, contributing to a smarter and more climate-adaptive future for agriculture.
details:
Problem

Climate change is making agricultural decision-making more difficult than ever. Rising temperatures, irregular rainfall, prolonged droughts, and soil degradation directly affect crop productivity, water availability, and long-term farm sustainability. Poor crop rotation choices can lead to nutrient depletion, increased erosion, and reduced resilience to environmental challenges.

Small and medium-sized farmers often have limited access to environmental data, technical support, and planning tools. While valuable scientific and Earth observation data already exist, they are not always easy to access or apply in day-to-day farm management.

As a result, farmers need practical tools that can transform complex environmental information into clear and actionable recommendations tailored to local conditions.

Proposed Solution

RasterRoot is a mobile decision-support platform that combines NASA environmental data, local farm information, and agronomic knowledge to help farmers choose and plan crop rotation strategies.

Using a multi-criteria evaluation model, the platform compares different rotation scenarios and identifies the best alternatives based on factors such as water availability, soil conservation, climate suitability, crop diversification, and operational feasibility. Recommendations are designed to support farmers in making more sustainable and resilient decisions while maintaining productivity.

Rather than replacing professional agronomic advice, RasterRoot provides accessible insights that help farmers better understand the opportunities and trade-offs associated with each strategy.

How It Works

Farmers begin by registering basic information about their property, including location, field size, crops, irrigation availability, and production priorities.

Using GPS or manual mapping tools, users define the boundaries of the field to be analyzed. The platform then processes environmental and agronomic indicators and presents the results through an intuitive dashboard with rankings, scores, visual charts, risk alerts, and technical reports that can be shared with stakeholders.

Key Features

  • Farm and field registration.
  • GPS and satellite-based field mapping.
  • Automatic area calculation and geospatial analysis.
  • Comparison of crop rotation strategies.
  • Indicators for water availability, soil health, erosion risk, and vegetation cover.
  • Technical report generation and sharing.
  • Portuguese and English language support.
  • Offline storage of up to 20 analyzed fields.

RasterRoot initially focuses on Uberlândia and the Triângulo Mineiro region of Brazil, promoting climate-smart agriculture through accessible scientific data and practical decision support.

NASA Data Used

RasterRoot uses NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) as its primary environmental data source.

The platform incorporates variables such as air temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, solar radiation, and other climate indicators to characterize local growing conditions and support crop rotation planning.

Local Data and Agronomic Knowledge

NASA data are complemented by information provided directly by farmers, including farm size, land use, crop history, irrigation availability, and production priorities.

The platform also incorporates agronomic knowledge related to water requirements, climate suitability, soil management practices, crop diversification, and operational feasibility. Technical references from EMBRAPA and Brazil's Agricultural Climate Risk Zoning Program (ZARC) help support the assessment of alternative crop rotation strategies.

Combining Earth observation data with local knowledge helps avoid generic recommendations and ensures that analyses reflect the realities of each farm.

Limitations and Future Work

RasterRoot is currently a prototype, and its results depend on both the quality of local information and the resolution of available environmental data. NASA observations represent environmental conditions at specific spatial and temporal scales and should not replace direct field measurements.

The multicriteria model also relies on weights and parameters that require further validation with farmers, agronomists, and researchers. Therefore, recommendations should be interpreted as decision-support guidance rather than guarantees of success.

Future developments include agronomic validation of recommendations, sensitivity analysis of model parameters, support for additional crops, climate scenario assessments, improved offline functionality, and expansion to new agricultural regions.

Technologies and Tools

Backend & Integrations

  • C#
  • Microsoft Azure
  • Environmental data processing services

Mobile Application

  • React Native

SI - Assisted Development

  • Microsoft Copilot: coding assistance, image generation, and mathematical and statistical support (technically reviewed by a software engineer and a statistician) .
  • Claude and Grok: UI prototyping, storytelling, and visual asset creation.
  • ChatGPT: research support and agricultural reference analysis.
  • Lovable: final presentation video production.

Offline Capabilities

  • Local storage of analyzed fields.
  • Technical report sharing.
  • Portuguese and English support.
